svg.text: Two things called a lane
Phase 0 — plan-side execution lanes (left) and the CI lanes that verify them (right)
SENSE 1 · EXECUTION LANE — subtask dependency chain, grouped by target folder
SENSE 2 · CI LANE — a job in phase0-ci.yml
Lane A
contracts/
R1 profile · R1–R4 schemas · shared samples · byte-identity gate (last)
contracts-gate
python contracts/check_sync.py — 36 synced copies byte-identical, F2 grep clean
Lane B
V2X_ECU/
CMake toolchain · codec seam · VanetzaCpmCodec · gv_tool · golden vectors
v2x-core-build
cmake + ctest + the golden-vector determinism check (Vanetza deps cached)
Lane C
ADA_ECU/
C++ toolchain · R2/R3/R4 bindings · additive-version test · detector Python
ada-core-build
python-tests
cmake + ctest for the C++ core; pytest for the detector bindings
Lane D
Scenario_Player/
bench CpmContent dataclass · round-trip over the golden .json side
python-tests
pytest, guarded on requirements-dev.txt and tests/ existing
Lane E
IVI_ECU/
sealed Kotlin R4 binding · finalized R3 models · additive-version test
ivi-unit-tests
Gradle on temurin JDK 17 — the local JDK exceeds Gradle 8.13's range
Lane F
smoke test
netcheck tool → image push → Nydus deploy → View Log evidence
netcheck-image
builds and pushes the image; C1–C5 are observed on the platform, not in CI
Lanes are logical dependency structure, not concurrency — at run time every subtask executes sequentially in one working tree.
A CI lane lands before the code it verifies, guarded on file existence, so it stays green until its consumer arrives.
Phase 1 adds four jobs to the same file — v2x-comms-check · sp-codec-helper · v2x-ecu-image · scenario-player-image (10 jobs total).
Its plan-side lanes are V (V2X_ECU/) · P (Scenario_Player/) · D (deploy — user-manual, no CI lane).
Source: plans/phase0_tasks.md § Execution order · plans/phase1_tasks.md § Execution order · .github/workflows/phase0-ci.yml
